summary: Walpole Island Lower A32: a square concrete tower of 1931 in the South Channel of the St. Clair River, one of a pair of aids set up in 1920; recognized in 2015.

structures.note: Register: about 5.6 m (18.4 ft). Coast Guard list: 9.9 m for the structure above ground level. The sources disagree; the story gives both.

access.note: Offshore beside Walpole Island, a Walpole Island First Nation community. The sources describe no public route to the tower.

events.note: Upper A34 and Lower A32 established as a pair. The original pole lights were later replaced by reinforced-concrete towers, before a major dredging in the mid-1930s.
Recognized as a heritage lighthouse under the Heritage Lighthouse Protection Act, 29 May 2015.

notes_for_editor: Height conflict left open: register about 5.6 m against Coast Guard list 9.9 m above ground; the story gives both. No keeper or storm sources were found for this light. Not used: the Marine keepers' table entry for 'Chenal Ecarte range' (P. Willis, 1914-15 volume), because it refers to the northern range pair (CCG 746/747), not to A32/A34. The 1920-21 Marine report's Ontario new-aids list names 'Walpole island' but the entry is garbled in the OCR (reads 'tractor'), so it is not cited. The Parks Canada DFHD pages (pc.gc.ca/apps/dfhd) returned no text to the reader; register wording comes from HistoricPlaces.ca and Heritage Guide copies. The Marine corpus ends in 1924, so the 1929-1931 construction and mid-1930s dredging rest on the register alone. Photos: none mirrored for this light; Heritage Guide credits a 1932 photograph (Library and Archives Canada, PA-148237) of the Upper A34. Not used: Wikipedia and Wikidata (record only).
